newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Techs busy but talk is of Dow.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Techs busy but talk is of Dow.

text.p: Options on technology stocks were fairly busy Thursday as the underlying shares staged a recovery from recent losses, options traders said.

Several long term options also were active and traders said a big topic of conversation on trading desks was the licensing of new products based on the Dow Jones industrial average .DJI by Dow Jones & Co.
Earlier today, Dow Jones said it awarded licences on its 101-year-old market measure to the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT), Chicago Board Options Exchange (CBOE) and American Stock Exchange (AMEX).
"The main topic of conversation this afternoon has been the new Dow index products," said Hank Nothnagel, head of the options trading desk at Everen Securities.
"There are a lot of unkowns out there, but it has all the potential to be a dynamic product," he said.

Dow Jones said the AMEX will offer trading in an exchange- traded fund based on the industrial average, the CBOT will offer trading in futures contracts and options on futures contracts and the CBOE will offer trading in listed options contracts on the average.
Thomas Ascher, vice chairman of the CBOE, said the exchange could have an options product on the Dow industrials as early as this fall.

"We have to make certain that everything is properly addressed," he said. "We look at this as a partnership with Dow Jones and we have to make certain we're working in concert to allow the product to fulfil its potential."
Traders and other options and futures industry analysts said the new products would likely make their biggest splash with retail investors rather than institutional investors.
"When you look at the level of market participation by the public and afford them the opportunity to use this as a vehicle, it's very exciting," Ascher said.
Some options traders said the long-anticipated news from Dow Jones combined with the upcoming May U.S. employment report to keep trading overall on the quiet side.

The May jobless report is scheduled for release before the stock market opens Friday. Economists on average expect a rise in payrolls of 219,000, compared with a rise of 142,000 in April. Average hourly earnings are expected to be up 0.4 percent after a 0.1 percent decline in April.
Among individual options, activity was fairly heavy in some technology stock options, including Micron Technology Inc, Intel Corp and Compaq Computer Corp.

A few long term options, known as LEAPS, which stands for Long Term Equity Anticipation Securities, were busy, including the McDonalds Corp January 1998 45 call, which traded more than 6,600 contracts.
The Wal-Mart Stores Inc January 1998 22-1/2 call traded about 4,025 contracts and the AMR Corp January 1998 105 call traded 3,750.
